guide.title: How to use this system
guide.sub: From nothing to your first run — every page explained, one by one.
guide.shotHint: This section's screenshot has not been added yet — supply the file below:
guide.s1Body: It performs repetitive browser work for you. You record a task once — or build it on the canvas — and from then on you just press Run: the application opens a fresh tab, clicks through the pages, fills the forms from your spreadsheet, and writes the results back into that same file.
guide.s1Note: The order matters: create the data source first, design the process second, and install the browser extension last, because nothing can run until it is there.
guide.s2Body: The first page you see after signing in. The four cards across the top count your processes, data sources, actions and groups. Below them, the shortcuts make the common tasks a single click, and the two lists — recent processes and recent sources — show whatever you touched last.
guide.s2Caption: Dashboard: counts, shortcuts and recent work
guide.s3Body: Every process you own. Each row is one process, and its columns describe that process at a glance.
guide.s3L1: Title: the name you chose. Rename it from the pencil beside the title, or from inside the editor.
guide.s3L2: Last run, group count, action count and source: the process's state without opening it.
guide.s3L3: Actions column: edit, record, run or delete the process from here.
guide.s3Caption: Process list with search and the create button
guide.s4Title: The process editor (the heart of the system)
guide.s4Body: Pressing Edit on any process opens the editor: a large canvas where the workflow appears as boxes joined by arrows. The toolbox sits on the right — drag a box onto the canvas to add it. To connect two nodes, drag from one node's output dot to the next node; hold the pointer near a node's edge for its connection dots to appear.
guide.s4Caption: Editor: toolbox, canvas and process properties
guide.s4N1: Start: where the process begins, and where the data source, step delay and repeat mode are set. A process has exactly one.
guide.s4N2: Group: a set of steps that repeat together — for example once per spreadsheet row.
guide.s4N3: Condition: splits the path into a success branch and a failure branch.
guide.s4N4: Action: the actual work on the page — a click, a form field, a navigation, or a spreadsheet read/write.
guide.s4Note: If an edge loops back to an earlier node, each node re-runs at most as many times as the loop-back limit allows; if the exit condition is never met, the run stops with a clear message rather than spinning forever.
guide.s4P1: Title: the same name shown in the process list.
guide.s4P2: Step delay: a short pause after each step, for pages that load slowly.
guide.s4P3: Loop-back limit: the ceiling that prevents an endless loop.
guide.s4P4: Data source: the spreadsheet this process reads from and writes to by default.
guide.s5Body: A data source is a table the system reads from and writes to. You can upload your own spreadsheet or build the table by hand.
guide.s5L1: Each source is independent: deleting a process never deletes its data source, which stays in the library.
guide.s5L2: One row means one run of the process. The first row is normally the column headings.
guide.s5L3: The File column lets you view the table or download it as a spreadsheet.
guide.s5L4: When a source is attached to several processes, the Process column lists them all.
guide.s5Caption: Source library: columns, row count and export
guide.s6Body: Instead of fixed text you can put a dynamic value in the editor. These are resolved at run time from the data source, which is what lets one process serve every row of your spreadsheet instead of needing a process per row.
guide.s6Hint: Take the exact variable syntax from the help beside that field in the editor — the same pattern works in every editor field.
guide.s7Body: Recording and running both need a browser extension. This page shows the prepared folder path for the extension on this machine. It works in Chrome and Edge only.
guide.s7Caption: Extension page: path, versions and install steps
guide.s7S1: Press Copy path so the extension folder path is on your clipboard.
guide.s7S2: In the browser, open chrome://extensions (or edge://extensions).
guide.s7S3: Turn on Developer mode, press Load unpacked, and choose the path you copied.
guide.s7S4: Come back to the panel and refresh the page.
guide.s7Note: The Global extension covers both recording and running, so it is installed once. If you still have the older separate extensions, remove them first.
guide.s8Body: If you would rather not build the workflow by hand, record it instead: the system watches what you do and builds the boxes for you.
guide.s8S1: In the process list, press the record button on that row. A fresh tab opens.
guide.s8S2: Do your work in that tab: sign in, click, fill in the form.
guide.s8S3: Press the red REC button to stop. What you did is saved into the workflow as groups and actions.
guide.s8Note: Closing the tab ends the recording there and tells you so — nothing is left half-finished.
guide.s9Body: Pressing Run starts the process immediately: a fresh tab opens and the system works through the steps one by one.
guide.s9L1: You can pause a run and resume it.
guide.s9L2: If a page turns out different from what the process expects, the run stops rather than doing the wrong thing.
guide.s9L3: Values read from the spreadsheet, and the results of the work, are saved back into that data source, so your file is up to date.
guide.s10Body: If several customers or departments need the same workflow, publish it as a template. Each person creates their own copy in one click and picks only their own data source; the rest of the workflow follows the template. Editing the template updates every copy.
guide.s10Note: This page is shown to administrators and senior users only.
guide.s11Body: Complete your first name, last name, email and mobile number here — they are needed for notifications and for identifying your account. You can upload and crop a profile picture from this page too, and switch the panel language.
guide.s11Caption: Account settings: profile, picture and language
guide.s12Body: Every process and data source is stored on the server, not only in your browser. Signing in from another computer shows you the same processes. The browser's local copy exists only for speed; the real work happens on the server.

actions.SelectOption: Pick an option from a dropdown
actions.InsertContent: Write a value into a data-source cell
actions.LoadContent: Load a data-source cell into a target
actions.DeleteRow: Delete a row from a data source
actions.SetMemory: Store a value in a memory variable
actions.selectByHint: If no value matches exactly, the same text is tried as the visible label.
actions.setMemoryHint: This step's resolved value is stored in the variable for later steps.
actions.getMemoryHint: Reads the variable's value into this step's value. An unset variable reads as empty.
actions.deleteRowHint: The chosen row is removed from the source and the rows after it move up by one. This changes the stored source.
actions.waitForUrlLoad: Wait for the page to finish loading
actions.waitForUrlLoadHint: On (default): waits until the target page finishes loading. Off: the next step runs immediately.
actions.waitMaxMsHint: Upper bound for the load wait; if it takes longer, execution continues.
actions.aliasWrite: {list} all write the text into the field; only the name differs.
actions.aliasRead: Behaves the same as {list} - both read the field's text. Only the name differs.

actionDesc.NoAction: Does nothing; useful as a pass-through point in the diagram.
actionDesc.Hover: Keeps the pointer on the element so a hidden menu or tooltip opens.
actionDesc.Hold: Like a click, but the mouse button is held down for the configured duration.
actionDesc.InputContent: Fills the chosen element's field with the given value.
actionDesc.ClearContent: Empties the text of the chosen field.
actionDesc.SelectOption: Chooses one option inside a dropdown (select).
actionDesc.InsertContent: Writes the given value into one cell of a data source.
actionDesc.LoadContent: Reads one cell of a data source and writes it into a page element or a memory variable.
actionDesc.DeleteRow: Deletes one row from a data source and moves the following rows up.
actionDesc.SetMemory: Stores a value in a memory variable so later steps can use it.
actionDesc.GetMemory: Reads a memory variable; an unset variable reads as an empty value.
actionDesc.GoToUrl: Navigates the browser to the given address.
actionDesc.NewPage: Opens a new tab and navigates it to the address.
actionDesc.WaitTime: Waits for the given duration, then runs the next step.
actionDesc.WaitForLoading: Waits for the page to finish loading or for an element to appear.
actionDesc.ScrollPage: Scrolls the page up/down or to an element.
actionDesc.Breakpoint: Pauses the run so you can resume it by hand (to inspect mid-flow).
actionDesc.RemoveElements: Removes the chosen elements from the page.
actionDesc.LoadCaptcha: Used to load or solve a captcha.
actionDesc.unknown: Unknown action "{name}" - this build does not recognise that action type.
